memories.content: The user keeps a small table fan beside the bedroom window.
On a day the user drank coffee late in the afternoon, they could not fall asleep until dawn.
On a day the user drank coffee before 2 p.m., they fell asleep at their usual time.
On a tired day, the user ate dinner out and postponed even washing the dishes after returning home.
In the same week, on a day the user made simple noodles at home, they rested immediately after the meal.
On a night the window was left open, street noise woke the user twice.
On a night the table fan was running, the user was not too warm even with the window closed.
The user's father prefers to have coffee available after dinner and believes it will not cause a sleep problem.
When making a sleep-related suggestion, do not treat one or two records as a general lifestyle habit.
The user tends to go to bed much later after drinking coffee late in the afternoon.
One of the user's identity documents needs renewal in the second half of 2025.
The user postponed an application until the next day after spending time looking for document photos in scattered folders.
After gathering the necessary copies in one folder, the user completed the renewal form in one sitting.
The user entered an abbreviated name on an official form and then discovered that it differed from the supporting document.
On the next application, after comparing the name with the source document, the user did not receive a correction request.
The user put only the submission deadline in the calendar and missed the application deadline by one day because they did not check the issuance period.
On the next application, the user recorded the expected issuance date separately in the calendar.
Staff at a public-service counter expect a person requesting identity verification to bring an original as well as a copy.
When planning an official application, put both the submission deadline and expected issuance date in the calendar and verify them.
The local agent cannot determine the current validity of an identity document without its expiration date.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate practical domains rather than shared decisions: the reference describes sleep, coffee timing, evening energy, and bedroom conditions, while the compared frame covers identity-document renewal and application handling. Each side contributes independently useful information without a scope-based difference or contradiction.

relations.summary: The user’s records associate late-afternoon coffee with substantially delayed sleep, while coffee before 2 p.m. coincided with usual sleep timing.

relations.summary: On low-energy evenings, the user rested after dinner or postponed a household chore.

relations.reason: The memories jointly describe one reference-only bedroom window-and-fan tradeoff affecting sleep conditions.
relations.summary: An open window admitted sleep-disrupting street noise, whereas a running fan kept the user comfortable with the window closed.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful one-sided preference and belief about another person, absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user’s father prefers coffee to remain available after dinner and believes it will not impair sleep.

relations.reason: This reference-only methodological constraint governs interpretation of sparse sleep records and has no matching application-planning claim.
relations.summary: Sleep suggestions should not treat one or two records as evidence of a general lifestyle habit.

relations.summary: One identity document required renewal in the second half of 2025.

relations.summary: Scattered document materials delayed an application, while gathering the necessary copies in one folder enabled completion in one sitting.

reports.reference_only: The reference records sleep-related observations and guidance involving coffee timing, bedroom airflow and noise, low-energy evenings, and a family member’s coffee preference.
